simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to מָגוֹר (H4032) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 8 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: מָגוֹר (mâgôwr) means a fright (objective or subjective) First listed occurrence: Isa 31 9.

definitions.full: H4032. magor or magur מָגוֺר noun masculine fear, terror — absolute ׳מ Psa 31:14 6 t. + Jer 20:3 compare below; plural suffix מְגוּרַי Lam 2:22 ; — fear, terror Isa 31:9 ; = cause of terror Jer 20:4 ; elsewhere in phrase, coined by Jeremiah, ׳מ מִסָּבִיב terror on every side 6:25 ; 20:3 (where as proper name), 20:10 ; 46:5 ; 49:29 ; Psa 31:14 ; Lam 2:22 ( מִסּ ׳מְגוּרַי ).
definitions.rootNote: or (Lamentations 2:22) מָגוּר ; from 1481 in the sense of fearing ;
